page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance virtualized via KVM on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8475B processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz. System memory totals 32.0 GB, yielding a strict 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included in the configuration.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating network-attached block storage for operating system files and persistent data. Networking capabilities feature a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps, while public IPv4 connectivity requires manual allocation as zero complimentary public addresses are supplied.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the 1:2 memory-to-vCPU configuration minimizes unallocated memory overhead in compute-bound environments where raw processor capacity is the primary constraint. Workloads aligned with this resource balance include distributed compilation tasks, batch processing pipelines, web application serving, and computational engineering routines that do not demand extensive in-memory working sets or local storage arrays.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture. The instance is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8475B processor operating at 2.7 GHz, matched with 32.0 GB of system memory to maintain a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It contains no integrated GPU accelerators and provides no bundled local disk storage, relying on external network block storage for persistence. Network infrastructure delivers a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Designed for scenarios demanding processor throughput over large memory footprints, the instance offers cost-efficient compute density for compute-intensive workloads such as batch processing, code compilation, continuous integration pipelines, and front-end web serving.
